info.title: Chord API
info.description:
Chord teammates are AI agents that hold a conversation on your behalf. A teammate
answers from knowledge you give it, calls the tools its workspace has connected, and
hands off to a human when it should. This API is how your product talks to one.

You are integrating into a Chord tenant that already exists. Its owner issues you an
API key scoped to what your integration needs, so nothing here asks you to create an
account or manage credentials. What you do is send turns, read what came back, feed
the teammate knowledge, and wire your system to it in both directions.

**There is no sandbox.** Every call bills real usage, writes real records and fires
real webhooks. Build against a tenant you are willing to fill with test data.

## Authentication

Send your key as a bearer token on every request:

```
Authorization: Bearer chord_live_...
```

The key identifies the tenant, so you never pass a tenant id yourself.

The two receivers you call from your own system,
`POST /api/external-chat/webhook/{source_id}` and
`POST /api/events/webhook/{subscription_id}`, take no bearer token: they authenticate
on an HMAC signature instead. See Webhook signing below.

## Scopes

Permissions are matched as exact strings, so ask the account owner for the specific
scopes covering the endpoints you call. Wildcards such as `rag:*` are not expanded.

| To call | Ask for |
|---|---|
| `POST /v1/external-chat/messages`, `/v1/external-chat/messages/stream` | `orchestrator:chat` |
| Knowledge and document reads, `POST /v1/knowledge/search` | `rag:retrieve` |
| Knowledge writes: bundles, uploads, URL ingest | `rag:ingest` |
| Knowledge deletes | `rag:delete` |
| Teammate reads | `teammate:read` |
| Threads, turns, events, chat exports | `thread:read` |
| Webhook registrations | `webhook:read`, `webhook:create`, `webhook:delete` |
| `GET /v1/usage` | `usage:read` |

`webhook:create` is the write scope for the whole registration, including
`PATCH /v1/webhooks/{id}`, `POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/test` and
`POST /v1/webhooks/{id}/secret/rotate`. There is no `webhook:update`.

Scope required per endpoint: `docs/api-reference/permissions.md`.

## Models

You do not choose one. Chord's operator-owned route policy selects the provider
model and versioned retail tariff. Omit the retired public `model` field: a
nonblank value returns `400 MODEL_OVERRIDE_RETIRED` before provider work begins.

## Quality signal

Every chat response carries `input_quality` and `response_quality` (0.0 to 1.0) and a
`recommended_action` of `SEND`, `REVIEW`, `TAKEOVER` or `CLARIFY`. Use it to decide
whether to publish the answer straight to your user or route it past a human.

## Errors

```json
{
  "error": { "code": "UNAUTHORIZED", "message": "Invalid or expired API key", "status": 401 },
  "requestId": "3f0c1c2e-9a44-4a1e-b3f2-8d0a7c5e1b90"
}
```

- Branch on `error.code`. `error.message` is written for a human and can change; some codes pass a provider's own wording through verbatim.
- One code can arrive with different statuses (`FAILED_PRECONDITION` is 400, 409 or 422), so never key on a `(code, status)` pair.
- Four pairs mean the same thing: `FORBIDDEN`/`PERMISSION_DENIED`, `INTERNAL`/`INTERNAL_ERROR`, `SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE`/`UNAVAILABLE`, `GATEWAY_TIMEOUT`/`DEADLINE_EXCEEDED`. Handle each pair identically.
- `error.details`, a field-to-message map, appears only on body-validation failures. Treat it as optional on every code.
- Quote the `X-Request-Id` **response** header when reporting a problem. On 401, 403 and 429 it is the only identifier that correlates with anything.
- Two surfaces skip this envelope: an SSE stream reports failure as a terminal `error` event carrying a bare `{"code", "message"}`, and the signed `/api/*` receivers answer with a flat `{"error": "..."}`.

Full code catalog with retryability: `docs/api-reference/errors.md`.

## Rate limits

Each API key gets its own budget, 60 requests per minute by default. Rate-limited
paths carry `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining` and `X-RateLimit-Reset` on
success as well as on rejection, so you can slow down before you are throttled. Only
a rejection adds `Retry-After`.

More than one condition answers 429 and only one is worth retrying, so branch on
`error.code` rather than on the status:

| Code | Status | Retry? |
|---|---|---|
| `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` | 429 | Yes, after `Retry-After` seconds |
| `CREDITS_UNAVAILABLE` | 429 | No. Ask an admin to review workspace credits and execution availability; no `Retry-After` is provided |
| `MEMORY_CAP_EXCEEDED` | 429 | No. A stored-memory ceiling was reached; delete memories first |
| `PAYMENT_REQUIRED` | 402 | No. The workspace is out of credit |
| `LLM_QUOTA_EXCEEDED` | 503 | No. The upstream model provider refused on quota |

## Streaming

`POST /v1/external-chat/messages/stream` emits server-sent events named after the
stage that produced them (`tool_call`, `synthesizing`, `token` and so on), so there is
no single channel to subscribe to. Rebuild the answer by concatenating `info` across
`token` events.

- `done` is the only success terminator. A stream that ends without it failed: do not present the partial answer as final.
- A `:hb` comment arrives every 15 seconds. The wall-clock ceiling is 120 seconds.
- Authentication, validation and quota failures happen before the stream opens and come back as ordinary JSON with a normal status code, never as stream events.

Every event of every streaming endpoint: `docs/api-reference/streaming.md`.

## Pagination

List endpoints do not all page the same way, so read the response shape of the one
you are calling. Most carry either a cursor header (`X-Next-Page-Token`, with
`page_size` and `page_token` query params) or a cursor in the body (`next_cursor`
plus `has_more`, with `cursor` and `limit`). Cursor values are opaque: do not parse
them. Treat any list whose length equals the page size as possibly truncated, because
a few endpoints cap results without returning a cursor.

Per-endpoint conventions: `docs/api-reference/pagination.md`.

## Webhooks

Register a URL with `POST /v1/webhooks` and name the events you want. Matching is
exact string equality: there is no `booking.*` wildcard, and an unrecognised name is
accepted at registration and then simply never fires, so check your spelling.

The envelope, where `data` is per-event:

```json
{"id": "<event uuid>", "type": "booking.confirmed", "timestamp": 1800000000000, "data": {}}
```

`timestamp` is epoch milliseconds. The body bytes are frozen when the event is
queued, so a retry resends a byte-identical body.

Every delivery carries `X-Chord-Event` (the type), `X-Chord-Event-Id` (identical for
every subscriber of one event) and `X-Chord-Delivery-Id` (yours, stable across
retries: use it as your idempotency key). `X-Chord-Signature` is present when the
registration has a signing secret.

Delivery is 4 attempts backing off 1s, 10s, 60s, and a `Retry-After` on your response
lengthens the wait up to 5 minutes. Chord retries on network errors and on 408, 425,
429 and 5xx, gives up on any other non-2xx, and never follows a redirect. Retries are
not hard-capped, so deduplicate on `X-Chord-Delivery-Id`.

Events include `conversation.escalated`, the `procedure.*`, `escalation-rule.*`, `vertical.*` and
`booking.*` families, `delegation.completed`, `event.processed`,
`usage.threshold_reached` and `webhook.test`. Full catalog with payload keys:
`docs/api-reference/webhooks.md`.

### Webhook signing

**Two different HMAC-SHA256 schemes share the header name `X-Chord-Signature` and the
same `sha256=<lowercase hex>` value format.** Implement the one belonging to the
endpoint in front of you, or verification fails on every request:

| | Plain scheme | Timestamped scheme |
|---|---|---|
| Signed payload | the raw body, and nothing else | `utf8(timestamp + ".")` followed by the raw body bytes |
| `X-Chord-Timestamp` | absent | required |
| Replay window | none, deduplicate on `X-Chord-Delivery-Id` | plus or minus 5 minutes |
| Applies to | every delivery from a `/v1/webhooks` registration | the two `/api/*` receivers you call, and the external-chat callback Chord calls |

Which scheme applies does not follow the direction of the request, so branch on the
presence of `X-Chord-Timestamp` rather than on who is calling whom. On the
timestamped scheme a value below 1000000000000 is read as seconds and otherwise as
milliseconds; Chord's own callback sends seconds. Worked verifiers for both:
`docs/api-reference/webhooks.md`.

## Guides

The guides linked above sit in `docs/api-reference/`, beside `async-jobs.md`,
`external-chat.md`, `event-subscriptions.md` and `versioning.md`.

tags.name: Knowledge
tags.description: The material a teammate answers from. Create bundles, then upload files (PDF, DOCX, HTML, images) or point Chord at URLs. Documents are chunked, embedded and indexed; ingestion is asynchronous and reports progress through a job you poll.

tags.name: Search
tags.description: Semantic search across knowledge bundles, returning ranked passages with relevance scores. Useful for building your own retrieval UI over the same index a teammate answers from.

tags.name: Teammates
tags.description: The agents you talk to. A teammate carries a persona, the knowledge bundles it may read, the tools it may call and the guardrails it works under. Read them to discover which ids to send turns to.

tags.name: Teammate Schedules
tags.description: Recurring work a teammate performs on its own: daily digests, follow-ups, periodic reports. Each run produces a normal teammate turn.

tags.name: Threads
tags.description: The conversation record. Threads, their turns and their events cover every channel a teammate answers on, so an operator surface can read one inbox instead of one per channel.

tags.name: Chat Export
tags.description: Bulk export of a teammate's conversations as JSONL or CSV. The export runs as a job: start it, poll it, then download the result.

tags.name: Scheduled Tasks
tags.description: One queue for work a teammate should do later: a delayed message, a report to compile, a tool run to perform. Create tasks directly or let a teammate create them during a conversation.

tags.name: Procedures
tags.description: Step-by-step instructions (SOPs, runbooks) a teammate follows for a given scenario. Attach them to a teammate to encode your process instead of restating it in every prompt.

tags.name: Escalation Rules
tags.description: The conditions under which a teammate stops answering and hands the conversation to a human, and where that handover is announced.

tags.name: Escalation Notifications
tags.description: Per-teammate settings for who is emailed when a conversation escalates, and the link that email points at.

tags.name: Verticals
tags.description: Reusable behaviour templates: domain knowledge, tone and guardrails for an industry. Verticals inherit, so a narrow one can extend a broad one rather than repeat it.

tags.name: Memory
tags.description: Durable facts a teammate keeps about a customer across conversations. Extracted automatically during chat, and readable and editable here so you can seed or correct them from your own system.

tags.name: Artifacts
tags.description: Binary storage for images, voice recordings and documents a conversation produces or consumes. Uploads go through a presigned URL, so file size is not bounded by this API. Voice artifacts are transcribed so their contents are searchable as text.

tags.name: MCP Servers
tags.description: Connect an external MCP server to a workspace, authorize it with a token or OAuth, and discover its tools. Teammates with an empty MCP assignment list may use all enabled workspace servers; explicit server ids restrict them to selected servers. Each operation requires explicit MCP permissions.

tags.name: External Chat
tags.description: Bring your own messaging channel. Register a signed inbound webhook so your users' messages reach a teammate, and a signed outbound callback so replies (including a human operator taking over) return to the conversation they started in.

tags.name: Event Subscriptions
tags.description: Trigger a teammate from something that happened in your system. Register a signed webhook bound to a teammate and an instruction template; each event runs the instruction against the payload and reports the result back to you.

tags.name: Webhooks
tags.description: Receive events as they happen. Register a URL, choose the event types you want, and Chord delivers signed JSON with retries. Verify the HMAC-SHA256 signature on every delivery.

tags.name: Usage
tags.description: API calls and token consumption for your key, filterable by date range, so you can attribute cost inside your own product.

tags.name: Skills
tags.description: Original skill files, saved drafts and immutable published revisions

get.description: Returns a single MCP server by ID. Requires `mcp:read` permission.

put.description: Updates an MCP server. Only provided fields are changed. Requires `mcp:manage` permission.

delete.description: Permanently deletes an MCP server. Requires `mcp:manage` permission.

get.description:
Returns the workspace's provisioned bridge: its `source_id`, the inbound `webhook_path`, the outbound `callback_url`, and whether credentials are stored. Secrets are never returned.

A workspace with no bridge is **not** a 404: it returns 200 with the single field `{"status":"disconnected"}`. Branch on `status`, not on the HTTP code.

Requires the `connector:read` permission.

200.description: The provisioned bridge, or `{"status":"disconnected"}` when none exists

put.summary: Provision or update the external-chat bridge
put.description:
Creates the bridge on first call and updates it on later calls. The `source_id` is minted once and kept stable across updates, so the inbound `webhook_path` never changes.

**Credentials are write-only.** `signing_secret` is required on the first call; omit it later to keep the stored one. Each write that supplies a credential stores it under a fresh key and retires the previous one only after the new key is live, so a failed write never leaves the bridge pointing at a missing secret.

`callback_url` is required on every call and is validated against the outbound SSRF policy, so private, loopback and link-local destinations are rejected with a 400.

A successful call also marks the EXTERNAL_CHAT connector enabled for the workspace. Requires the `connector:manage` permission.

500.description: Credential storage or the settings write failed; the previously live bridge is left untouched

400.description: `callback_url` missing, `signing_secret` missing on first provision, or a `callback_url` the outbound SSRF policy refuses

delete.description:
Deletes the workspace's bridge row and its stored credentials. The `source_id` is retired with it, so inbound webhooks on the old `webhook_path` start failing authentication and a later re-provision mints a new one.

Idempotent: deleting a workspace that has no bridge is a 204, not a 404. Requires the `connector:manage` permission.

204.description: Bridge deleted, or there was none to delete

get.description: Returns a single vertical by ID. Requires `vertical:read` permission.

put.description: Updates a vertical by ID. Uses optimistic concurrency control -- pass `expected_version` matching the vertical's current version. Requires `vertical:update` permission. Fires `vertical.updated` webhook.

409.description: Version conflict -- the vertical was modified since you last fetched it

delete.description: Permanently deletes a vertical by ID. Fails with 409 if the vertical has children. This action cannot be undone. Requires `vertical:delete` permission. Fires `vertical.deleted` webhook.

get.summary: Get a teammate's escalation notify address
get.description: The email address notified when one of this teammate's conversations escalates to a human. `notify_to` is null when not configured (feature off). Requires `teammate:read` permission.

put.summary: Set a teammate's escalation notify address
put.description: Enables escalation email notifications for this teammate: on a real agent-to-human takeover, an email with the recent transcript and a dashboard link is sent to `notify_to`. Upsert semantics (re-PUT replaces the address). Requires `teammate:update` permission.

delete.summary: Clear a teammate's escalation notify address
delete.description: Disables escalation email notifications for this teammate. Idempotent: 204 whether or not a setting existed. Requires `teammate:update` permission.

get.description: Returns a single teammate by ID (UUID) or email address. Requires `teammate:read` permission.

put.description: Updates a teammate's configuration by ID (UUID) or email. Supports incremental updates to bundles, channels, and MCP servers via add/remove/set fields. Requires `teammate:update` permission.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a teammate by ID (UUID) or email. The teammate will no longer handle conversations or appear in teammate lists. This action cannot be undone. Requires `teammate:delete` permission.

get.description: Returns the teammate's per-agent connector-tool scope — the set of connector tool types (e.g. "bookings", "menu", "notion") this teammate is allowed to use. An EMPTY list with `unscoped=true` exposes ALL workspace-enabled connector tools (back-compat); with `unscoped=false`, no connector tools are enabled. The identifier can be either the teammate's **email** or **ID** (UUID). Requires `teammate:read` permission.

put.description: Replaces the teammate's per-agent connector-tool scope with `enabled_tool_types`. The runtime then exposes only the INTERSECTION of (workspace-enabled connectors) AND this set. Set `unscoped=false` with an empty list to disable all connector tools. Omit `unscoped` and pass an **empty list to clear the scope** — the teammate becomes unscoped and again sees ALL workspace-enabled connector tools (back-compat). The identifier can be either the teammate's **email** or **ID** (UUID). Requires `teammate:update` permission.

put.summary: Save original file changes without changing live replies

get.description: Returns the teammate's current playbook (persona prompt). The identifier can be either the teammate's **email** or **ID** (UUID). Requires `teammate:read` permission.

put.description:
Sets the teammate's playbook — a structured prompt that defines how the teammate
carries out its daily tasks. The playbook is stored as the teammate's persona and
is injected into every conversation as the system prompt.

If the teammate has a workspace, this endpoint also triggers **automatic extraction**
of timezone, business hours, and bookable resources from the playbook via LLM analysis.
Extraction runs asynchronously (2-5 seconds) after the HTTP 200 response is returned.
On success, a `workspace.config_extracted` webhook is fired. On failure, a
`workspace.config_extraction_failed` webhook is fired. Extracted config is merged
into the workspace config: keys the extraction produced overwrite the current
values, keys it did not produce are left untouched. To change an extracted value,
edit the playbook text and PUT it again.

The identifier can be either the teammate's **email** or **ID** (UUID).

Requires `teammate:update` permission.

get.description: Returns a single procedure by ID, including its full text, tags, and attached teammates. Requires `procedure:read` permission.

put.description: Updates a procedure by ID. Uses optimistic concurrency control -- you must pass `expected_version` matching the procedure's current version. Tags can be incrementally added/removed via `add_tags` and `remove_tags`. Requires `procedure:update` permission. Fires `procedure.updated` webhook.

409.description: Version conflict -- the procedure was modified since you last fetched it

delete.description: Permanently deletes a procedure by ID. The procedure is automatically detached from all teammates. This action cannot be undone. Requires `procedure:delete` permission. Fires `procedure.deleted` webhook.

get.description: Returns a single knowledge bundle by ID, including its access control settings. Requires `rag:retrieve` permission.

put.description: Updates an existing knowledge bundle's name, description, or access control. Requires `rag:ingest` permission.

delete.description: Permanently deletes a knowledge bundle and all its documents and vector embeddings. This action cannot be undone. Requires `rag:delete` permission.

get.description: Returns a single escalation rule by ID, including its condition, action, and attached teammates. Requires `escalation-rule:read` permission.

put.description: Updates an escalation rule by ID. Uses optimistic concurrency control -- you must pass `expected_version` matching the rule's current version. Requires `escalation-rule:update` permission. Fires `escalation-rule.updated` webhook.

409.description: Version conflict -- the rule was modified since you last fetched it

delete.description: Permanently deletes an escalation rule by ID. The rule is automatically detached from all teammates. This action cannot be undone. Requires `escalation-rule:delete` permission. Fires `escalation-rule.deleted` webhook.

get.description: Returns memories for a teammate with optional filters and cursor-based pagination. Requires `memory:read` permission.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Maximum number of results per page

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: Opaque cursor for pagination. Obtained from a previous response.

post.description: Creates a new memory entry for a teammate. Memories represent facts, preferences, observations, or notes learned about customers. Performs content deduplication. Enforces a cap of 1000 memories per teammate per workspace. Requires `memory:create` permission.

429.description: Memory cap exceeded (max 1000 per teammate per workspace)

get.description: Returns all MCP servers for a workspace. Requires `mcp:read` permission.

post.description: Adds an external MCP server to the workspace. Requires `mcp:create`. Use `bearer` for an Authorization bearer token, `api_key` for the X-API-Key header, `none` for unauthenticated access, or `oauth` followed by the OAuth authorization flow. Auth tokens are stored securely and never returned. Empty or omitted `enabled_tools` allows all discovered tools. No explicit teammate assignment is written. Enabled servers are available to teammates whose MCP server assignment list is empty.

409.description: Server name already exists in workspace

post.description: Discovers the MCP server's tools and input schemas. Static bearer/API-key tokens are loaded only for enabled servers; enable a static-auth server before an authenticated probe. Requires `mcp:read`. OAuth servers must be connected before discovery. This returns the server's available tools; `enabled_tools` controls which are available to a teammate.

409.description: OAuth server not connected or token service unavailable

post.description: Starts OAuth with PKCE for a registered server using `auth_type=oauth`. Requires `mcp:manage`. Open the returned authorization URL in a browser for consent; the API call alone does not connect the server. The connection is shared by the workspace. State is single-use and expires after 10 minutes.

parameters.name: redirect_uri
parameters.description: Absolute HTTPS callback URL on a deployment-approved origin. HTTP is allowed only for loopback development. The callback receives the provider's code and state; submit them to authenticated OAuth completion.

502.description: Server missing, not configured for OAuth, or OAuth discovery or client registration failed

400.description: Invalid or disallowed redirect URI or server URL

post.description: Exchanges the authorization code received at your redirect URI and stores the provider tokens securely. Requires `mcp:manage` in the same tenant that started the flow. The state must match the workspace and server and is consumed once, including on failure. Do not retry completion with a consumed state; start a new flow.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: The one-time state returned by OAuth start

parameters.name: code
parameters.description: Authorization code received at the redirect URI

403.description: Missing permission or flow belongs to a different tenant

400.description: Invalid, expired or consumed state, or code exchange failed

post.description: Tests connectivity by listing tools. Static bearer/API-key tokens are loaded only for enabled servers; enable a static-auth server before an authenticated probe. Requires `mcp:read`. A completed probe returns HTTP 200 even when connectivity fails; inspect `status` (`ok`, `error`, or `timeout`) and `error` in the response.

get.description: Returns every subscription registered for the workspace, newest first, wrapped in a `subscriptions` array. Not paginated: the per-workspace cap of 50 is the bound. Signing secrets are never returned. Requires the `connector:read` permission.

post.description:
Mints a `subscription_id` and returns the `webhook_path` the external system should POST signed events to. The `signing_secret` you supply is the shared HMAC key for that endpoint; it is stored by reference and never returned, so record it now.

Subscriptions are immutable: there is no update endpoint. To change the teammate, instruction template or filter, delete the subscription and create a replacement (which mints a new `subscription_id`, so the webhook path changes too).

A workspace holds at most 50 subscriptions. Creating one also marks the EVENT_SUBSCRIPTION connector enabled for the workspace. Requires the `connector:manage` permission.

409.description: The workspace already holds the maximum of 50 subscriptions. A failure to store the signing secret currently surfaces here too.

post.description: Returns a presigned S3 URL for uploading an artifact. Upload the file directly to S3 using the returned URL, then call the confirm endpoint to finalize. Requires `artifact:create` permission.

Confirms that an artifact has been uploaded to S3. Call this after successfully uploading the file using the presigned URL. Creates the artifact metadata record. Requires `artifact:create` permission.

400.description: Invalid request (missing s3_key, name, or media_type)

get.description: Returns all webhook registrations for the specified tenant, including their status and subscribed events. Requires `webhook:read` permission.

post.description: Registers a new webhook endpoint to receive real-time event notifications. If a `secret` is provided, every delivery includes an `X-Chord-Signature: sha256={hmac}` header for verification. Failed deliveries are retried 3 times with exponential backoff (1s, 10s, 60s). Requires `webhook:create` permission.

401.description: Missing or invalid API key / tenant_id

post.description: Durably queues a test event and returns immediately.
Returns the new secret once. It is never included in later reads.

get.description: Returns verticals for the authenticated tenant with optional filters. Supports category filtering and cursor-based pagination. Requires `vertical:read` permission.

parameters.name: page_size
parameters.description: Maximum number of results per page

parameters.name: page_token
parameters.description: Opaque cursor for pagination. Obtained from a previous response.

post.description: Creates a new vertical (domain behavior template). Verticals define free-form domain context for teammates. Supports inheritance via parent_id (child content is appended to parent). Requires `vertical:create` permission. Fires `vertical.created` webhook.

get.description: Returns threads scoped to (tenant, workspace), ordered by last_turn_at desc. Filterable by channelId, agentId, controlState, dateRange, and free-text search. Cursor-paginated via last_turn_at.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Inclusive lower bound on last_turn_at (epoch ms)

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Inclusive upper bound on last_turn_at (epoch ms)

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Free-text search on preview / remote name

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Pagination cursor: the prior page's next_cursor (opaque; legacy bare epoch-ms also accepted)

parameters.name: needs_review
parameters.description: Trust loop: only threads whose review_state == needs_review

parameters.name: max_confidence
parameters.description: Trust loop: only threads whose latest agent turn scored at or below this confidence

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Lifecycle filter: open | archived. Absent = no filter (both).

post.description: Creates a thread for outbound-first (proactive) conversations before the customer has sent anything. v1 accepts channel_id "external_chat" only; the workspace must have external-chat settings provisioned (404 EXTERNAL_CHAT_NOT_CONFIGURED otherwise) — the bridge source_id is resolved from them, never from the body, and is the stable internal thread key. session_id is kept only as the provider-facing reply route; when omitted, sender_id is used. The requested teammate must be the teammate configured on the bridge. Returns 201 with the thread; re-posting an existing (channel, source, sender) key with the same teammate and reply route returns 200 with the existing thread unchanged. A conflicting owner or reply route, or a key held outside the workspace, is a 409 THREAD_ROUTE_CONFLICT. Requires thread:write.

409.description: THREAD_ROUTE_CONFLICT — the (channel, bridge source, sender) key is already in use outside this workspace or has a different teammate or provider reply route.

200.description: The (channel, bridge source, sender) key already exists in this workspace with the same teammate and reply route; the existing thread is returned unchanged.

201.description: Created — a new empty thread was inserted.

post.summary: Submit operator feedback on an agent turn (trust loop)
post.description: Records a thumbs-up/down verdict plus an optional correction on a single agent turn. A thumbs-down flags the thread for follow-up (review_state=needs_review); a thumbs-up signs it off (review_state=reviewed). Idempotent on (tenant, thread, turn, operator) — re-rating the same turn overwrites the prior verdict. Requires thread:write. Body: {rating: "up"|"down", correction_text?: string, operator_user_id?: string}.

delete.summary: Clear operator feedback on an agent turn (trust loop)
delete.description: Removes the calling operator's prior verdict for (tenant, thread, turn, operator) — the backend unset for the FE's feedback-thumb toggle-off (Living Canvas Phase 5). Mirrors the POST's auth/scoping/validation: agent-turn-only, tenant/workspace scoped, requires thread:write. Idempotent — clearing a verdict that was never set returns 200 (no-op), not 404. Scoped to the calling operator: another operator's verdict on the same turn is left intact. The thread's review_state is left as-is (a cleared verdict doesn't re-open or sign off a thread). Body (optional): {operator_user_id?: string} — defaults to the API key id.

post.summary: Operator takes control of a thread
post.description: Flip control_state from agent_active or paused to human_active, then send a fixed recipient acknowledgement. Returns the updated thread and acknowledgement delivery status.

post.summary: Resume a paused thread back to agent_active
post.description: Flip control_state from paused to agent_active. To resume with operator control instead, call /take-over.
Sets status=open, resuming with whatever control_state the thread had when it was closed. Idempotent — reopening an open thread returns it unchanged. Requires thread:write.

- **resume** / **activate** → teammate returns to normal operation, subject to the workspace activation rule (ADMINS_ONLY by default). These actions cannot clear a governed suspension.

post.summary: Send a message and get the agent reply inline (sync)
post.description:
Injects a customer-style message into an external-chat thread, runs the
agent, and returns its reply in the same HTTP response. The turn persists
like any other channel turn (visible on `GET /v1/threads` and
`GET /v1/threads/{id}`), so operators can take over later. No outbound delivery
happens — the reply travels back here, not through the connector's sender.

Every provider execution uses the shared workspace billable-execution lifecycle.
With prepaid enforcement enabled, its assigned workspace pool is admitted before
model dispatch; suspended API principals are blocked, and the completed turn
produces one durable usage record.

### Starting vs continuing a conversation
The thread is keyed by `(external_chat, session_id, sender_id)` within your
`workspace_id`:
- **Continue** an existing conversation: send the **same** `sender_id` **and**
  `session_id` as before — the message appends and the agent sees prior turns.
- **Start a new** conversation: use a **new** `session_id` (recommended: a
  fresh UUID per conversation) or a different `sender_id`.

⚠️ If you omit `session_id` it defaults to the literal `"sync"`, so all
messages from the same `sender_id` land in one shared thread. Always pass a
distinct `session_id` if you want separate conversations.

### Outcomes
- Agent replied → `{ thread_id, reply, agent_invoked: true, steps }`. `steps`
  lists the tools the agent executed (same shape as the chat API's `steps`:
  tool name, success, latency, citations/structured payload); it's an empty
  list when the agent answered without invoking any tools.
- A gate stopped the turn (thread is `human_active`/paused, or the agent
  produced nothing) → `200` with `{ thread_id: null, reply: null,
  agent_invoked: false, reason: "no_reply", steps: null }`. The inbound
  message still persisted.

Requires a Bearer token with the `orchestrator:chat` permission.

502.description: `ORCHESTRATOR_ERROR`: the agent failed to produce a reply (upstream LLM/orchestrator error).

200.description: Processed. Either the agent reply (`agent_invoked: true`) or a no-op outcome (`agent_invoked: false`, `reason` set, e.g. `no_reply`).

403.description: Token lacks `orchestrator:chat`, is scoped to another workspace, or its governed principal is suspended

503.description: `DISABLED`: the endpoint is off. A governed admission or operator-pricing dependency may also be temporarily unavailable before provider work starts.

post.summary: Send a message and stream the agent reply (SSE)
post.description:
Streaming variant of `POST /v1/external-chat/messages`. It uses the same
workspace billable-execution, pool, and API-principal policy as the synchronous
endpoint before opening an SSE stream. Same request body and the **same
conversation-identity rules** —
the thread is keyed by
`(external_chat, session_id, sender_id)` within `workspace_id`, so reuse both
to continue a conversation and change `session_id` (or `sender_id`) to start a
new one. Omitting `session_id` defaults it to `"sync"`.

The response is a `text/event-stream`:
- `event: token` — repeated; `data` is the next reply delta.
- `event: done`  — terminal; `data` is `{ "thread_id", "agent_invoked",
  "steps" }`, where `steps` lists the tools the agent executed (same shape
  as the chat API's `steps`; empty when no tools ran).
- `event: error` — on failure; `data` is `{ "error" }`.
- SSE comment heartbeats (`:hb`) keep the connection warm across tool
  round-trips.

Auth and validation run **before** the stream opens, so `4xx`/`5xx` are
returned as plain JSON; once the stream is open, failures arrive as an
`error` event. Requires a Bearer token with `orchestrator:chat`.

400.description: `INVALID_REQUEST` (returned as JSON before the stream opens): `workspace_id`, `sender_id` and `text` are required.

403.description: Token lacks `orchestrator:chat`, is scoped to another workspace, or its governed principal is suspended

200.description: SSE stream opened (`text/event-stream`). Reply arrives as `token` events then a terminal `done` event.

503.description: `DISABLED`: the endpoint is off. A governed admission or operator-pricing dependency may also be temporarily unavailable before provider work starts.

post.description:
Signed entry point for one inbound customer message. No API key is used: the path is exempt from gateway authentication and the HMAC signature is the only credential.

## Signing contract

Send both headers (they are matched case-insensitively):

- `X-Chord-Timestamp` — epoch time as an integer. A value below `1000000000000` is read as **seconds**, anything at or above it as **milliseconds**. Chord's own outbound callback sends seconds.
- `X-Chord-Signature` — `sha256=<lowercase hex>`.

The preimage is the timestamp, a literal `.`, then the request body:

```
signature = "sha256=" + lowerhex(HMAC_SHA256(signing_secret_utf8,
                utf8(timestamp + ".") || raw_request_body))
```

Concatenation happens on bytes, so sign the exact bytes you transmit — do not re-serialize the JSON before signing. The secret is the `signing_secret` you supplied when provisioning the bridge.

## Replay window

The timestamp must be within **±5 minutes** of server time (`chord.connector.external-chat.inbound.max-skew-ms`, default `300000`). Outside that window the request is rejected before the signature is even checked.

## Not the same as Chord's outbound webhook signature

Tenant webhooks registered through `/v1/webhooks` reuse the header name `X-Chord-Signature` and the same `sha256=<hex>` format, but sign the **raw body alone** with no timestamp. The presence of `X-Chord-Timestamp` is the only wire-level marker separating the two schemes. Implement this one for this endpoint.

## Delivery semantics

Bodies are capped at 256 KiB. Chord verifies, routes, claims the idempotency key `{source_id}:{message_id}`, enqueues, and returns 200 — all before the agent runs. The reply is delivered later as a signed POST to the bridge's `callback_url`.

## Lifecycle events

An optional `type` field selects the event kind. `session_closed` archives the conversation instead of delivering a message: it is verified, deduplicated and applied synchronously, acking `{ok, processed}` (`text` is not required; `sender_id` and `message_id` still are). A close for a conversation Chord has never seen acks `{ok, ignored: unknown_thread}` without consuming the idempotency key, so redeliver it after the conversation's first message to apply it. Any other `type` value — absent, `message`, or unrecognized — delivers an ordinary customer message, exactly as if the field were not sent. A later message for a closed conversation reopens it automatically.

Retry on 5xx: a 503 means a transient condition (channel disabled, resolver unavailable, circuit breaker open, queue full) and your redelivery will be processed. Do **not** retry a 401: unknown `source_id`, a disconnected bridge, a stale timestamp, a bad signature, and a body missing `sender_id`, `message_id` or (for messages) `text` all land there and none of them get better on retry.

parameters.name: X-Chord-Timestamp
parameters.description: Epoch seconds (below 1000000000000) or milliseconds. Must be within ±5 minutes of server time.

parameters.name: X-Chord-Signature
parameters.description: `sha256=` followed by lowercase-hex HMAC-SHA256(secret, utf8(timestamp + ".") || raw body).

requestBody.description: The inbound message. Sign these exact bytes.

400.description: The request body could not be read

503.description: Transient: webhook disabled, no resolver configured, circuit breaker open, a signing-secret or datastore outage, or the inbound queue is full. Retry.

401.description: Rejected: unknown or disconnected `source_id`, missing or stale `X-Chord-Timestamp`, bad signature, unparseable JSON, or a body missing `sender_id`, `message_id` or `text`. Terminal, do not retry.

200.description: Authentic. `{ok, queued}` when the message was accepted onto the inbound queue; `{ok, processed}` when a `session_closed` lifecycle event was applied synchronously; `{ok, ignored}` when it was authentic but deliberately dropped, where `duplicate` means the idempotency key `{source_id}:{message_id}` was already claimed, `tenant_suspended` means the tenant is suspended, and `unknown_thread` means a `session_closed` referenced a conversation Chord has never seen (that ack does not consume the idempotency key — redeliver later). A 200 means Chord accepted responsibility for the delivery, not that the agent has answered: message turns run asynchronously and the reply arrives as a signed POST to the configured `callback_url`.

type.description: Event type. Optional: `session_closed` archives the conversation resolved from the bridge `source_id` + `sender_id`; `session_id` is reply-routing metadata, not Chord thread identity. `text` is not required for it, and the ack is `{ok, processed}` (or `{ok, ignored: unknown_thread}` when the conversation was never seen; redeliver after its first message to apply the close). Any other value — absent, `message`, or unrecognized — delivers an ordinary customer message, exactly as if the field were not sent. A later message for a closed conversation reopens it automatically.

text.description: The customer's message text. Required. Also accepted as `message`.
text.example: Hi, can I move my booking to Friday?

sender_id.description: Stable identifier for the end customer. Required. Also accepted as `senderId` or `customer_id`. Together with the bridge `source_id`, this is the stable Chord thread identity.

message_id.description: Provider-unique id for this message. Required. Also accepted as `messageId`. Forms the idempotency key `{source_id}:{message_id}`, so a redelivery with the same value is acked 200 with `ignored: duplicate` rather than processed twice.

session_id.description: Conversation/session identifier on the external system. Optional: also accepted as `conversation_id`, and defaults to `sender_id` when the provider has no conversation concept. Preserved as the provider callback route; changing it does not create a new Chord thread for the same bridge and sender.

sender_display_name.description: Human-readable name for the sender. Optional: also accepted as `sender_name` or `display_name`.

is_group.description: Whether the message came from a group chat rather than a one-to-one thread. Optional, defaults to false. Also accepted as `group`.

ExternalChatInboundMessageDto.description: One inbound delivery — a customer message, or (via `type`) a session lifecycle event. Fields may be sent at the top level or nested under a `data` object: when `data` is present and is an object, it is read and the top level is ignored. `sender_id` and `message_id` are always required, and `text` is required for messages (a blank or missing one is a 401, not a 400, because an unparseable body is indistinguishable from a forged one at this layer). Unrecognized fields are ignored.

error.description: Short machine-readable reason. `rejected` on 401; `body too large` on 413; `read error` on 400; and on 503 one of `webhook disabled`, `no inbound resolver configured`, `service overloaded`, `resolver unavailable`, `route unavailable` or `queue full`.

InboundWebhookError.description: Failure body for a signed inbound webhook. These endpoints sit outside the gateway's error envelope, so they return a bare `{"error": "..."}` object with no `code`, `status` or `requestId` field.

queued.description: Present and true when the delivery was accepted onto the inbound queue.

ignored.description: Present instead of `queued` when the delivery was authentic but deliberately not processed. `duplicate` means the channel's idempotency key was already claimed; `tenant_suspended` means the tenant is suspended, so the delivery is acked and dropped rather than left to retry-storm; `unknown_thread` means a session lifecycle event referenced a conversation Chord has never seen (redeliver after the conversation's first message to apply it).

processed.description: Present and true when the delivery was a lifecycle event handled synchronously (e.g. external-chat `session_closed`): the effect is already applied and there is no queued work to await.

InboundWebhookAck.description: Ack for an authentic inbound delivery. Exactly one of `queued`, `processed` or `ignored` is present. A 200 means Chord accepted responsibility for the delivery, not that the agent has finished with it: queued work runs asynchronously and its outcome is reported on the channel's own return path, not on this response.

event_type.description: The event's type. Also accepted as `type` or `event`. Required only when the subscription sets an `event_type_filter`, which is matched against it case-insensitively and exactly. A mismatch is rejected with 401.

event_id.description: Provider-unique id for this event. Also accepted as `id`. Optional: when absent Chord derives `sha256:<hex>` from the raw body, so byte-identical redeliveries still deduplicate. Forms the idempotency key `{subscription_id}:{event_id}`.

EventWebhookPayloadDto.description: One external event. Chord reads only the two fields below; every other field is passed through to the agent verbatim, so send whatever context the teammate needs. The whole body is embedded in the agent prompt as JSON and truncated at 16000 characters. Treat the payload as untrusted input: the run it triggers executes with customer-channel restrictions and without the pre-approved-autonomy framing that trusted scheduled runs get.

Unauthorized.description: Missing, malformed, revoked or expired API key. Codes: `UNAUTHORIZED`, `UNAUTHENTICATED`. Not retryable.

Forbidden.description: Authenticated, but not permitted. Codes: `FORBIDDEN` and `PERMISSION_DENIED` (your key lacks the scope; handle both identically), `TENANT_SUSPENDED` (the account is suspended and its owner must resolve that), `EMAIL_VERIFICATION_REQUIRED`, `FEATURE_DISABLED`, `TENANT_MISMATCH`. Not retryable.

PaymentRequired.description: Code `PAYMENT_REQUIRED`: the workspace has no credit left, so the run was refused. Retry once the account owner has topped it up.

RateLimited.description: Throttled or capped. Branch on `error.code`, not on the status: `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` is retryable after `Retry-After` seconds, while `CREDITS_UNAVAILABLE` (workspace execution unavailable) and `MEMORY_CAP_EXCEEDED` (hard capacity ceiling) are not and carry no `Retry-After`.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying. Present on `RATE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED` only.

X-RateLimit-Limit.description: Maximum requests allowed in the current window.

X-RateLimit-Remaining.description: Requests left in the current window. Also sent on successful responses.

X-RateLimit-Reset.description: Seconds until the current window resets.

ServerError.description: Unexpected failure. Codes `INTERNAL` and `INTERNAL_ERROR`, which mean the same thing and both carry a fixed generic message. Quote the `X-Request-Id` response header when reporting one.

ApiKey.description: The API key issued to you by the account owner. Format: `chord_live_...`
